summary.en: Afghan Taliban forces opened fire on Pakistani security forces along the Kurram border, prompting an intelligence-led army response that killed a Pakistani officer and several terrorists in Balochistan. Pakistan suspended trade at two Iran border crossings, citing security and smuggling concerns, while trade with Afghanistan fell sharply after border closures. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. These actions intensify cross-border violence and economic pressure beyond the school roof collapse previously reported.
summary.nb: Afghanske Taliban-styrker skjøt mot pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker langs Kurram-grensen, noe som førte til et etterretningsledet hærrespons som drepte en pakistansk offiser og flere terrorister i Balochistan. Pakistan stanset handel ved to grenseoverganger mot Iran, med begrunnelse i sikkerhets‑ og smuglingsbekymringer, mens handelen med Afghanistan falt kraftig etter grenselukkinger. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP. Disse handlingene intensiverer grenseoverskridende vold og økonomisk press utover kollapsen av skoletaket som tidligere ble rapportert.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
